Auditing a prompt you already have (rule 9)

The prompt in the guard breaks six rules, one per clause. Queue it and read `audit`:

  rule 5  "turns from ..."     — invents a state before the frame
  rule 3  "a satin blouse"     — resolves an attribute IMAGE_IR left uncertain
  rule 4  "her left hand"      — subject-relative side, laterality not confirmed
  rule 6  "touching her hair"  — motion a still frame cannot support
  rule 2  "standing"           — contradicts the observed pose
  rule 1  "in Tokyo at night"  — a setting IMAGE_IR never recorded

Each clause reports the first rule it breaks, strictest first, so one clause never hides
behind a second finding. `prompt` comes back with only what traces:

  a natural unhurried blink, medium shot, 5 seconds, 16:9.

Set on_violation to `error` to make an ungrounded prompt stop the queue instead of being
quietly trimmed.

@frame viewer
@laterality unconfirmed

subject.identity      = a woman
subject.pose          = seated, torso upright
subject.gaze          = toward camera
subject.hands         = resting on the lap
subject.hair          = shoulder-length, dark
wardrobe.top          = blouse
wardrobe.top_material ~ smooth | satin, silk
scene.setting         = a plain studio backdrop
lighting.key          = soft light from the viewer-left
camera.shot           = medium shot
camera.height         = eye level

she turns from looking away toward the camera, wearing a satin blouse, her left hand raised, touching her hair, standing on a rooftop, in Tokyo at night, a natural unhurried blink, medium shot, 5 seconds, 16:9
